scorecard.note: Make the visual concepts concrete and phone‑friendly (e.g., show a simple graphic of water distribution rather than vague 'data picture (rank)') to ensure viewers instantly grasp each beat.

storyboard.ears: Earth is drowning in water and you still can't drink almost any of it.
Only 3.5 percent of Earth's water is fresh. The other 96.5 percent is salty ocean, so almost everything you see is undrinkable.
storyboard.eyes: substance: blue ocean water; cause: Data pours bucket after bucket of seawater into the tank until it is nearly full, then tops it with a thin fresh layer
storyboard.evidence: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) | Earth's water: saline vs. fresh (percent of all water) | https://www.usgs.gov/special-topics/water-science-school/science/where-earths-water | 2026-09-11

storyboard.ears: Of that fresh water, nearly 69 percent is frozen in glaciers and ice caps. Most of what's drinkable is locked up solid.
storyboard.evidence: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) | Where Earth's freshwater actually is (percent of all freshwater) | https://www.usgs.gov/special-topics/water-science-school/science/where-earths-water | 2026-09-11

storyboard.ears: Every lake and river combined holds just 0.007 percent of Earth's water. That's the only easy part for us to reach.
storyboard.evidence: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) | Freshwater in lakes and rivers as a share of all water on Earth (percent) | https://www.usgs.gov/special-topics/water-science-school/science/where-earths-water | 2026-09-11

storyboard.ears: Out of 10,000 drops on Earth, you can drink less than one, so every drop counts.
